div.div: 7 انفثّ , inf. n. اِنْفِثَاثٌ, i. q. اِنْكَسَرَ [accord. to the TK used in its proper sense as signifying It broke, or became broken: but for this I find no authority]. (T, O, K.) So in the saying, انفثّ الرَّجُلُ مِنْ هَمٍّ أَصَابَهُ [The man became broken in spirit, or languid, from anxiety, or solicitude, that befell him]. (T, O.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
